name: Matt Schulte

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Schulte lists his occupation as musician, filmmaker and philosopher.
Schulte's pamphlet statement lists his background as founder of Lower Boom and Clarosophy and adjunct professor at WSU and PNCA.
bio.excerpt: Founder, Lower Boom; Founder, Clarosophy; Adjunct professor WSU and PNCA

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Schulte says downtown Portland is a resource the city should develop, not just a problem to be solved.
positions.excerpt: Downtown Portland is not just a problem to be solved. It is, in fact, a resource we should develop.

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Schulte says the Northwest needs far more electrical capacity than it currently has.
positions.excerpt: the Northwest needs far more electrical capacity than it currently has.

positions.statement: Schulte's pamphlet statement describes a proposed 'Grid-Connected Core' that would partner with building owners to put downtown buildings back to work.
positions.excerpt: The Grid-Connected Core partners with building owners to put those buildings back to work

positions.statement: Schulte's pamphlet statement describes a proposed 'ReBoot' effort connecting volunteers and professionals to help people navigate existing services.
positions.excerpt: ReBoot connects volunteers and professionals to help people navigate existing services

positions.statement: In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Schulte says he would require a citywide strategic plan before the next budget.
positions.excerpt: I would require a citywide strategic plan before the next budget,

positions.statement: In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Schulte says the city should implement the 911 Call Allocation Working Group's recommendations within one year.
positions.excerpt: We should implement the 911 Call Allocation Working Group’s recommendations within one year

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report.
